clue.text: Hit hard, society suffering setback

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the pieces before it are read from right to left

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A club or society takes a heavy blow and suffers a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' turns H + SOC round as one string, giving the four letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to strike someone with a cudgel is to hit them hard.

clue.text: One aloof army officer meets beauty, female to be hugged

parts.note: COL is short for colonel

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside, so the letter goes within the beauty word

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A reserved colonel meets a stunning woman who wants a cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an unemotional, unfriendly person is likened to a chilled fish.

clue.text: Undertake to get some lamb from the butcher?

definitions.meaning: to take on a burden or responsibility
a cut of lamb, the upper foreleg joint sold by butchers

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to bear a responsibility, and a joint of meat cut from the foreleg.

clue.text: Lusty older bod written about by journalist

indicators.note: 'about' signals that the letters of the words just before it are moved around into a new order

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: An ageing body is described in print by a reporter as lusty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' rearranges OLDER BOD into REDBLOOD; the editor follows, 'by' marking the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vigorous, virile, full-blooded person is described as lusty.

clue.text: Register name to participate in learning, having turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up reads the letters from bottom to top
participating means taking part within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone signs up to take part in a course after finally arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: N inside LORE gives LORNE, which 'having turned up' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to sign up officially for a course or membership.

clue.text: VIP that would do for many a mouse?

definitions.meaning: a very important person, a top dog

definitions.text: that would do for many a mouse?
definitions.meaning: a large piece of cheddar or similar, the food mice are fabled to love

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an important, influential person; literally a large cheese a mouse would enjoy.

clue.text: Past the difficulty, having negotiated traffic controller?

definitions.meaning: through the hardest part of a task
having driven across a speed bump, a ridge that slows traffic

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: once the worst part is behind you, the rest is downhill.

clue.text: Name of film actor with evidence of domestic neglect at home?

parts.note: dust gathers in an untended house
IN means at home

explanation.surface: A film star's house shows signs of neglected housework.
explanation.walkthrough: Dustin Hoffman is the American film actor in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the first name of Hoffman, star of The Graduate and Rain Man.

clue.text: Notice erected on building that's wrecked

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another comes above it
in a down entry something erected stands upright, so it is read bottom to top

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
a shed is a simple building

explanation.surface: A sign put up on a ruined building.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'erected' turns the notice so it reads upwards, and 'on' places it above the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hopes that are dashed are smashed or ruined.

clue.text: See work as something endlessly coming around?

parts.note: LO is an old word meaning look or see
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A puzzled musing on whether labour is a never-ending cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a closed circuit has no end and keeps returning to its start.

clue.text: Given initial publicity, more than one horrible female advances

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, i.e. publicity
ogresses are female monsters, plural

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant women, once given early press coverage, move ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given initial' tells you the publicity comes first, before the monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to move forward or make headway is to advance.

clue.text: In autumn restaurant won't have cold Middle Eastern dish

indicators.note: 'In autumn' places the next piece inside the season's word

parts.note: FALL is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: refusing to have something means leaving it out, so a letter drops from the eatery

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A seasonal eatery refuses to serve a chilled Middle Eastern dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'autumn' is the American word for the season, and 'In' sets the trimmed eatery inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: deep-fried balls of ground chickpea are a staple of Levantine cooking.

clue.text: Get to taxi before this promising beginning?

definitions.meaning: an aircraft taxis along the runway before taking to the air
a good start that bodes well

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an excellent start to an undertaking, from aviation or a running start.

clue.text: Emergency communication system abused in hotel

indicators.note: something abused is mistreated or knocked about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An emergency phone line in a hotel has been misused.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a direct telephone link kept open for urgent calls, such as between governments.

clue.text: Agree, once pupils have been lined up?

definitions.meaning: to concur or share the same view

definitions.text: once pupils have been lined up?
definitions.meaning: the pupils of the eyes literally aligned with each other

explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' looks like schoolchildren in a row; it means the dark centres of the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: when two people share a view they are said to look at it in the same way.

clue.text: Offering dinner, get cooking

indicators.note: cooking turns ingredients into something new, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An invitation to a meal, with an instruction to start preparing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tender is to offer formally, as with a bid or resignation.

clue.text: Chemical condition limits ability to discern sounds

indicators.note: to limit is to bound on all sides, so the condition word goes round the other

parts.note: a state is a condition
an ear for music is an ability to pick out sounds

explanation.surface: A medical condition restricts someone's hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a salt or ester of stearic acid, a chemical compound used in soaps.

clue.text: Genuine sweetheart to regret nothing after termination of engagement

indicators.note: the regret and nothing come after the letter taken from engagement
the termination of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to rue is to regret
LOVE is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A broken engagement leaves a sincere lover with no regrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the one person you love sincerely, a real beloved.

clue.text: Wrong conclusion? Run question a different way

indicators.note: putting the words a different way means reordering their letters

explanation.surface: Advice to rephrase a question that has led to a faulty deduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'it does not follow': an inference that does not follow from its premises.

clue.text: Jack joins members of the family for trips

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards
aunts are relatives

explanation.surface: A man named Jack goes on outings with his relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: short pleasure excursions are outings or trips.

clue.text: One offering reflections in newspaper

definitions.meaning: a looking glass shows your reflection
the Daily ... is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a glass that shows images back, and the name of a British tabloid.

clue.text: Sneeze being audible in dispute

indicators.note: something audible is heard, so the sneeze's sound gives the letters

parts.note: ATISHOO is the British written form of a sneeze, like achoo

explanation.surface: A loud sneeze breaks out in the middle of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a matter under debate or being argued over is the point in question.

clue.text: Path taken by one in British company aircraft

indicators.note: the path is taken along by what precedes it, so it follows on
'one in' puts the numeral inside the company's letters

parts.note: BP is the British oil company
I is the Roman numeral one
a lane is a narrow path or track

explanation.surface: A flight path used by an aircraft belonging to a British firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a two-winged aeroplane of the early aviation era is one kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Something extra that's good for France and America

parts.note: BON is French for good
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Something that benefits both France and the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an extra payment or benefit beyond what is expected.

clue.text: Relations hurried back with food supplies maybe

indicators.note: 'back' reads the word for hurried from right to left

parts.note: ran means hurried
rations are fixed allowances of food

explanation.surface: Family members rushed home carrying provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like family; it means accounts or tellings. RAN turned 'back' gives NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a relation is an account or telling of events, as in relating a story.

clue.text: Villain, one given a bash

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to have a bash is to have a go

explanation.surface: A bad guy takes a swing at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: IAGO is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Shakespeare's treacherous ensign in Othello is a famous stage villain.

clue.text: Good person with heart picking up speed as planner

indicators.note: picking something up takes it in, so the speed word goes inside

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the crossword's good person
the gist is the heart or essence of a matter
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted person who speeds up turns out to be an organiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good person with heart' is a charade of saint and essence, which 'picking up' opens to take the speed word in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who devises plans and tactics, especially in war or business.

clue.text: It's in another environment? Yes and no!

definitions.text: It's in another environment? Yes and no!

indicators.note: 'It's in' says the word lies inside the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether something is present in another place or not.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sits within 'anotHER Environment', so it is in another place, yet it names this place: hence 'Yes and no!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradox: the word means in this place, while it is tucked inside a phrase about elsewhere.
